answer: To sell from an orchard, each identity files a quill-signed receipt, locks 70, and pays 10. One key files one receipt per batch; bridge auditors match receipts to crates first. The bridge log lets anyone verify one receipt per batch; unmatched receipts burn the 70 escrow. The k-th fake needs its receipt, escrow, and fee, so 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 and pay 10,000. A receipt-rental ring fails: a rented quill signature binds to its key and batch, so reuse mismatches the audit, burning both escrows. An honest agent files once, pays 80, and recovers its escrow on delivery.
